title: Albany: cooking for musicians at Charlie Miller's restaurant
summary: From Buffalo she went to Albany and worked in Charlie Miller's restaurant, cooking red beans, rice and spareribs for the musicians who packed the place. She later cooked for the Basie band in theatre dressing rooms.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: You said you stayed a couple of years and then you said you had to go back home?
Yes. No, from Buffalo we went up to Albany.
I opened up a little restaurant up there.
Yeah. I used to live up there. Charlie Miller, he had a restaurant where all the musicians used to come there to eat.

But the only thing, he never fixed the things like they like. He wanted to fix what he wanted to fix, and they used to ask me. 'Helen, why don't you come on over', because I used to just cook for the musicians all the time. So Charlie asked me one time, and I wasn't working no place then, and he said, 'why don't you come on into business with me?' He wanted me to work for him. I said, 'well that would be

We used to have those real happy parties. I'd just cook the hot rolls and things. I used to get off work and they used to come. I would be upstairs sleeping and Charlie would call and he's say, 'here's all the musicians'. I said, 'okay, I'll be right down'. And I'd come on down. You know, I enjoyed doing some things. Like when I got with the big Basie Band. I cooked all over the United States in all the big theatre dressing rooms, you know, cooking for the band.
